title: Catégorie des types de mots [dont arbres plans] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Γ is a 'circular graph', i.e. a ribbon graph or combinatorial map. Its darts (oriented edges) form a set A⃗. σ0 is the edge-reversal involution and ρ_s is the cyclic rotation of darts around each vertex. Cutting the surface X along |Γ| gives a surface with canonical boundary. That boundary is a topological polygon, or a disjoint union of polygons if Γ is more general. Grothendieck now builds this boundary 'contour' C purely combinatorially from (A⃗, σ0, ρ_s).

Step 1. Edges of C correspond bijectively to darts of Γ: rd: A⃗ ≅ A(C), with a⃗ ↦ 'the right-hand side of a⃗' (he corrected 'gauche' to 'droite'). Each edge of C thereby gets a natural orientation.

Step 2. The darts of C are therefore A⃗(C) ≅ A⃗ × {±1}. The reversal involution of C is σ0^C ≅ id × τ, where τ swaps ±1. The parts are A⃗(C)_+ = rg(A⃗) and A⃗(C)_- = rd(A⃗).

Step 3. It remains to define the vertex involution σ1^C of C. A vertex of a contour is 2-valent, so σ1^C is an involution. It is defined separately on the two parts by turning around the vertices of Γ:
- σ1^C(rd a⃗) = rg(ρ_s^{±1} a⃗);
- σ1^C(rg a⃗) = rd(ρ_s^{∓1} a⃗).
The composite rotation ρ^C = σ1^C σ0^C on C is then given by rd a⃗ ↦ rd(ρ_s a⃗) and rg a⃗ ↦ rg(ρ_s^{-1} a⃗). Up to his conventions, the cycles of C are the orbits of ρ_s∘σ0, i.e. the faces (boundary components) of the ribbon graph.

Step 4. C is oriented, which gives a splitting A⃗(C) → {±1} with A⃗(C) ≅ A⃗(C)_+ × {±1} and σ0^C ≅ id × τ. So the datum σ1^C is equivalent to a single permutation of A⃗(C)_+ ≅ A⃗, namely a⃗ ↦ σ1^C σ0^C(a⃗). This is the boundary/face permutation of C.

Step 5 (point b, unfinished). C carries a fixed-point-free involution on its set of edges, with A⃗ = A⃗(C)_+, which reglues paired sides. This is the standard presentation of the surface as polygon(s) with sides identified in pairs.

Purpose within cote 152: for a plane tree the contour is a single polygon with 2n sides, i.e. the contour/Dyck word of the tree. This links 'arbres plans' to 'types de mots'.
errors: σ0^C is first written σ0 × τ, then correctly id × τ. Reversing an edge of C only flips the sign; it does not move the underlying dart. The first version is a slip.

In the boxed formula, rg(ρ_s^{-1}(a⃗)) is equated with σ0^C rd(ρ_s(a⃗)). Since σ0^C rd(b) = rg(b), this would give rg(ρ_s a⃗), so the exponents ±1 are inconsistent. This is probably an unresolved convention slip, partly crossed out.
Notation for the induced face permutation (ρ_C, ρ^C) is not stabilised; much of the middle of the page is struck out and illegible.

ideas.what: Boundary contour of a ribbon graph built combinatorially: edges of the contour ↔ darts of Γ via 'right side of the dart'; faces = cycles of rotation∘reversal
ideas.modern_name: faces/boundary cycles of a combinatorial map (σ0, σ1, σ2 = (σ1σ0)^{-1}); fat-graph boundary components
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter (1891), Edmonds (1960), Tutte; Jones–Singerman (1978); Penner/Kontsevich for fat graphs
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), cartes and dessins as pairs of permutations; more detail in unpublished notes

ideas.what: Surface obtained by cutting along the graph is a polygon (or polygons) whose sides are glued by a fixed-point-free involution
ideas.modern_name: polygon (side-pairing) presentation of a surface from a map

ideas.what: Orientation of the contour as a splitting A⃗(C) ≅ A⃗(C)_+ × {±1}, reducing σ1^C to one permutation on A⃗

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard combinatorial-map computation: the boundary of a ribbon graph read off from darts, with faces as orbits of rotation∘reversal. It is well known since Edmonds/Tutte/Jones–Singerman. The intended application, the contour word of a plane tree, is also classical (Harris, 1952). Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'σ0×τ [?]' should be read as a first, superseded version; later on the page it is 'σ0^C ≃ id×τ'.

Left margin first NB: likely 'NB A⃗(C)_+ est une orientation de C' (choice of orientation of the contour), accompanied by a small trivalent-vertex sketch with arrows indicating the right-hand sides of darts.
Boxed formula exponents (ρ_s vs ρ_s^{-1}) are uncertain in the image and possibly corrected by hand; the transcription's 'rg(ρ_s^{-1}(a⃗)) = σ0^C rd(ρ_s(a⃗))' is internally inconsistent as written.
'ρ_C^? = τ{a⃗ → σ1^C(σ0^C(a⃗))}' is likely 'ρ_C = la permutation {a⃗ ↦ σ1^C(σ0^C(a⃗))} sur A⃗'.
